title: Ash and the Whispering Woods
markdown:
The moonbeams lay like soft white pillows over the sleepy hills. Ash, a little elf with eyes as soft and deep as still water, smoothed his simple clothes. He felt a quiet, happy flutter inside. Tonight was a special night for a slow walk in the whispering woods. He wanted to ask the Old Pine Tree a gentle question that had been nuzzling in his mind for a long, long time.

Sitting on a low, mossy branch near Ash was Corvus, a crow with feathers as dark and shiny as the deepest night. Corvus ruffled his feathers. "Are we ready, Ash?" he murmured, his voice a low, mellow sound. "My chart is ready, you know. Though, it does look a little… swirly. More like a soft cobweb than a plain path!"

Ash smiled a slow, soft smile. Corvus’s chart, with its swirls and dots, was always a wonderfully swirly thing, more of a feeling than a plain drawing. "Yes, Corvus, we are ready. The Old Pine Tree is waiting for us," Ash whispered, his voice as soft as a tiny leaf falling.

And so, with a soft rustle of leaves under their small feet and wings, they started their slow walk into the heart of the quiet woods. The air felt cool and smelled of pine needles and soft, damp earth. The wood made little chiming sounds all around them, each tiny needle seeming to sing like a tiny bell in the gentle, whispering wind. Ash loved this quiet time of night, when the world felt hushed and full of sleepy secrets, when even the shadows seemed to be dreaming.

"Left here, Ash, left!" whispered Corvus, pointing a sleek black wing towards a path that seemed to wind deeper into the hushed, silvered shadows. "My chart says… well, it says something about a shiny rock that winks, and then a turn past a very sleepy mushroom that dreams of soft dew."

As they walked along, their path became a little less clear. The chiming sounds of the wood seemed to swirl around them in a gentle, soft swirl. Corvus looked closely at his chart, then up at the tall, old trees. His sleek black brow looked a little puzzled. "Hmm. This looks more like a patch of plump berries than a shiny rock. And that mushroom over there seems wide awake! Maybe my chart is a little… smudged, or maybe it has taken a little nap itself," he admitted, his usual strong voice softening into a gentle, almost sorry whisper.

Just then, a warm, buttery, and wonderfully comforting smell drifted towards them, as sweet as honey and as welcome as a cozy hug. Rounding a bend in the path, which was indeed becoming less certain, they saw a small, cozy house nestled amongst the trees. A kind baker, Bartholomew, with white flour like soft snow on his round cheeks, was polishing a row of gentle, glowing lanterns that cast a soft, friendly light. His smile was as warm as his freshly baked bread, and his eyes twinkled like far-off stars.

Ash felt a little flutter of quiet worry about his gentle question for the Old Pine Tree, and Corvus’s increasingly swirly chart was adding to the soft feeling. "Excuse me, sir," Ash whispered, his voice soft and polite, like the quiet sound of a small stream. "We are trying to find the Old Pine Tree. Do you happen to know the clearest way to get there from here?"

Bartholomew chuckled, a sound like smooth pebbles rolling in a gentle stream, a happy, rumbling sound. He looked kindly at Corvus’s smudged, swirly chart. "Ah, a muddled chart, I see!" he said with a warm chuckle. "The Old Pine Tree is much easier to find if you simply follow the stream. It flows right past its great, wise roots. The stream is always clear, you see, and it never gets swirly like some charts do when they are trying to be too clever!" He then reached into a basket and offered Ash a warm, buttery roll, its wonderful smell filling the air. "This will give you courage for your gentle question, young elf," he added with a wink.

Ash gratefully took the roll, its warmth spreading through his small fingers and into his heart. The buttery smell was lovely. "Oh, thank you, Bartholomew! A clear stream sounds much, much better than a swirly chart!"

Corvus nodded his sleek head a lot, letting out a happy, soft caw. "Yes, a stream! Much more sensible! No more squinting at smudges!"

With new confidence, the comforting warmth of the buttery roll, and Bartholomew’s simple, clear directions, Ash and Corvus followed the gentle sound of flowing water. They soon heard the soft murmur of the stream growing louder, and there it was – the big Old Pine Tree, its ancient, wise branches reaching out like gentle arms towards the softly glowing moon. Ash whispered his gentle question to its rustling, whispering needles, and received a soft, reassuring answer that settled deep within his heart like a warm, smooth stone.

The walk back felt peaceful and wonderfully clear, the chiming pinewood now familiar and welcoming. As the first soft, rosy light of dawn painted the eastern sky, they arrived back at their cozy, familiar home, feeling safe, content, and very, very ready for a good, long rest, knowing that sometimes, the clearest path is the simplest one, and a little bit of kindness can make any journey smoother and softer. Soon, they drifted off to sleep.
characters: Ash the young elf, a crow
